name: Warhammer 40,000
description: Warhammer 40,000 is the dominant sci-fi tabletop wargame, pitting Space Marines, Orks, Tyranids, and other factions against each other in grimdark future combat.
scaleNotes: Games Workshop uses heroic proportions — heads, hands, and weapons are intentionally oversized for visual impact at tabletop distance. The '32mm' label is a community convention; Primaris models measure closer to 40mm to helmet top.
printingTips: 0.2mm nozzle at 0.06mm layer height gives the best facial detail. FDM works well for vehicles and terrain. Resin is preferred for infantry heads and small detail parts.
popularWith: Competitive wargamers, lore enthusiasts, army builders, painters

name: Warhammer Age of Sigmar
description: Warhammer Age of Sigmar is Games Workshop's fantasy wargame set in the Mortal Realms, featuring Stormcast Eternals, Orruks, and daemonic factions.
scaleNotes: Same scale and proportions as Warhammer 40,000. Models are fully interchangeable between systems at the same base size.
printingTips: Same settings as 40k. Large centerpiece models like Kragnos print well on FDM at 0.2mm layers.
popularWith: Fantasy enthusiasts, painters, narrative gamers

name: Warhammer: The Old World
description: Warhammer: The Old World revisits the classic Old World setting with Bretonnia and Tomb Kings, using the traditional 28mm scale of the original Warhammer Fantasy Battles.
scaleNotes: Returns to the 28mm scale that Warhammer Fantasy Battles used before Age of Sigmar. Compatible with classic metal and plastic miniatures from the 1990s-2010s range.
printingTips: 28mm rank-and-file infantry prints quickly on FDM. Character models benefit from resin for fine detail like heraldry and faces.
popularWith: Old-school hobbyists, historical fantasy fans, rank-and-file wargamers

name: Middle-earth Strategy Battle Game
description: The Middle-earth Strategy Battle Game recreates battles from The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit trilogies with individually named heroes and troops.
scaleNotes: 28mm scale with proportions closer to realistic anatomy than the heroic 40k/AoS style. Models emphasize character accuracy over tabletop visibility.
printingTips: Resin is ideal for hero models with fine detail. FDM works for cavalry, monsters, and terrain pieces.
popularWith: Lord of the Rings fans, skirmish gamers, painters

name: Bolt Action
description: Bolt Action is the most popular 28mm World War II wargame, covering all major theaters and factions from 1939-1945.
scaleNotes: True 28mm heroic scale. Historical accuracy matters — vehicles at 1:56 scale match the infantry proportionally.
printingTips: 28mm infantry prints well on FDM. 1:56 vehicles (tanks, jeeps, trucks) are the FDM sweet spot for detail and speed.
popularWith: History buffs, WWII enthusiasts, diorama builders

name: Dungeons & Dragons
description: Dungeons & Dragons is the world's most popular tabletop roleplaying game. Miniatures are optional but widely used for tactical combat encounters.
scaleNotes: 28mm is the traditional scale, though official WizKids miniatures range from 25mm-32mm. Creature sizes follow the D&D size categories: Tiny through Gargantuan.
printingTips: FDM at 0.2mm layers works for medium and large creatures. Small and tiny creatures benefit from resin printing.
popularWith: RPG players, DMs, dungeon terrain builders, collectors

name: Star Wars: Legion
description: Star Wars: Legion is a mass-battle miniature game set in the Star Wars universe, featuring plastic miniatures for帝国, Rebels, and other factions.
scaleNotes: 35mm total figure height (top of head). Eye-level is closer to 32mm. Some community sources debate whether 35mm refers to eye-level or total height.
printingTips: Large vehicles like AT-ATs and AT-STs print beautifully on FDM. Infantry benefits from 0.2mm nozzle for facial detail at 35mm.
popularWith: Star Wars fans, cinematic wargamers, diorama builders

name: Star Wars: Shatterpoint
description: Star Wars: Shatterpoint is a skirmish game focused on hero-scale combat with larger, more detailed miniatures than Legion.
scaleNotes: 40mm scale, same as Marvel: Crisis Protocol. Larger than Legion to allow more dynamic poses and detail on individual heroes.
printingTips: 40mm heroes are large enough for FDM to handle facial detail. Use 0.2mm nozzle at 0.06mm layer height for best results.
popularWith: Star Wars fans, skirmish gamers, display painters

name: Marvel: Crisis Protocol
description: Marvel: Crisis Protocol is a tabletop miniatures game where players build crews of Marvel superheroes and villains for cinematic battles.
scaleNotes: 40mm scale (40mm to eye level, ~1:43 ratio). Previously listed as 35mm in some databases — corrected to 40mm based on community measurement.
printingTips: 40mm character models print well on FDM with a 0.2mm nozzle. Large characters like Hulk benefit from 0.4mm nozzle for speed.
popularWith: Marvel fans, skirmish gamers, display painters

name: Malifaux
description: Malifaux is a character-driven skirmish game set in a gothic steampunk alternate dimension where gremlins, zombies, and wizards clash.
scaleNotes: 32mm heroic scale, same as Warhammer 40k. Wyrd's aesthetic is more stylized with exaggerated features for characterful models.
printingTips: 32mm is forgiving on FDM. The stylized proportions mean small imperfections are less noticeable than on realistic sculpts.
popularWith: Narrative gamers, steampunk fans, competitive players

name: Infinity
description: Infinity is a fast-paced sci-fi skirmish game with anime-influenced aesthetics, featuring detailed metal and plastic miniatures.
scaleNotes: 28mm scale but with slim, anime-influenced proportions. Models tend to be leaner than the heroic proportions of Warhammer.
printingTips: Infinity models have very fine weapons and antenna details. Resin is strongly recommended for infantry. FDM works for terrain and Tags (mechs).
popularWith: Competitive skirmish gamers, anime fans, painting enthusiasts

name: Flames of War
description: Flames of War is the leading 15mm (1:100) World War II wargame, covering company-level battles across all theaters.
scaleNotes: 1:100 scale (15mm). Bases represent squads and teams, not individual figures. Armor and artillery are the primary focus.
printingTips: 1:100 vehicles print well on FDM. Infantry is very small and benefits from resin. Tank barrels may need pinning.
popularWith: WWII history enthusiasts, competitive wargamers, army builders

name: Warmachine & Hordes
description: Warmachine and Hordes are companion steampunk fantasy wargames featuring steam-powered warjacks and monstrous warbeasts in head-to-head combat.
scaleNotes: 30mm heroic scale — between 28mm and 32mm. Models are stockier than Warhammer with exaggerated weapons and armor.
printingTips: 30mm Warmachine figures print well on FDM. Warjacks (large steam robots) are excellent FDM subjects at 0.2mm layers.
popularWith: Competitive wargamers, steampunk fans, tournament players

name: Frostgrave & Stargrave
description: Frostgrave is a fantasy skirmish game set in a frozen city of lost magic. Stargrave is its sci-fi companion game set in a galaxy of scattered colonies.
scaleNotes: 28mm scale. Both games use the same core rules and are fully compatible at 28mm scale.
printingTips: 28mm is ideal for FDM printing. Terrain pieces like frozen ruins and sci-fi corridors print beautifully at 0.2mm layers.
popularWith: Skirmish gamers, terrain builders, narrative players

name: Kings of War
description: Kings of War is a mass-battle fantasy wargame with ranked units, designed as an alternative to Warhammer Fantasy Battles.
scaleNotes: 28mm scale. Mantic's own miniatures are 28mm heroic, and the game is fully compatible with any 28mm fantasy range.
printingTips: 28mm infantry and cavalry print well on FDM. Large monsters and siege equipment benefit from 0.2mm nozzle for detail.
popularWith: Mass-battle gamers, army builders, fantasy enthusiasts

name: BattleTech
description: BattleTech is a tactical wargame where players control giant robotic combat vehicles called BattleMechs in turn-based combat.
scaleNotes: 6mm scale (also called 'epic' scale). BattleMechs range from 8mm to 25mm tall depending on weight class. The game uses hex-based movement.
printingTips: 6mm Mechs are small but chunky — FDM handles them well. Use 0.2mm nozzle and print multiple Mechs at once for efficiency.
popularWith: Sci-fi wargamers, lore enthusiasts, tactical gamers

name: Dropzone Commander
description: Dropzone Commander is a 10mm sci-fi wargame featuring fast-paced combined-arms combat with infantry, tanks, and dropships.
scaleNotes: 10mm scale. Infantry are tiny but vehicles are substantial. The game emphasizes transport mechanics and urban combat.
printingTips: 10mm vehicles are great FDM subjects. Infantry is very small and benefits from resin. Buildings and terrain are the FDM sweet spot.
popularWith: Sci-fi wargamers, mass-battle fans, terrain builders

name: Legions Imperialis
description: Legions Imperialis brings the Horus Heresy to epic scale, with massive armies of Space Marines, Titans, and tanks clashing across war-torn battlefields.
scaleNotes: 8mm scale. Larger than BattleTech Mechs but smaller than 15mm. The game uses the same epic-scale system as Adeptus Titanicus.
printingTips: 8mm infantry is small but manageable on FDM. Titans and large vehicles are excellent FDM subjects. Use 0.2mm nozzle for infantry detail.
popularWith: Epic-scale fans, Horus Heresy enthusiasts, army builders

name: Grimdark Future
description: Grimdark Future is a free, miniatures-agnostic sci-fi wargame by One Page Rules. Use any miniatures you own — no specific range required.
scaleNotes: 32mm scale, compatible with any 28-32mm sci-fi miniatures. The game is designed to be model-agnostic, so any manufacturer's miniatures work.
printingTips: Since the game is miniatures-agnostic, print whatever you like. FDM at 0.2mm layers works well for most 32mm figures.
popularWith: Casual gamers, army builders, 3D printing enthusiasts

name: Fallout: Wasteland Warfare
description: Fallout: Wasteland Warfare brings the post-apocalyptic Fallout video game universe to the tabletop with detailed miniatures and narrative-driven scenarios.
scaleNotes: 32mm scale, same as Warhammer 40k. Features Power Armor, Brotherhood of Steel, Super Mutants, and other iconic Fallout factions.
printingTips: 32mm is forgiving on FDM. Power Armor and Vertibirds are chunky models that print well. Use 0.2mm nozzle for facial detail on humanoid figures.
popularWith: Fallout fans, narrative gamers, post-apocalyptic enthusiasts

name: Gaslands
description: Gaslands is a tabletop wargame for modified toy cars in a post-apocalyptic vehicular combat setting. Customize Hot Wheels and Matchbox cars into war machines.
scaleNotes: 1:56 scale, matching standard Hot Wheels and Matchbox cars. Compatible with 28mm wargaming terrain and accessories.
printingTips: 1:56 is the FDM sweet spot for weapons, armor, and accessories for toy car conversions. Print weapon mounts, roll cages, and armor plates.
popularWith: Kitbashers, post-apocalyptic fans, Hot Wheels customizers

name: Kill Team
description: Kill Team is Games Workshop's sci-fi skirmish game set in the Warhammer 40,000 universe, where small squads of specialists fight tactical missions.
scaleNotes: Uses the same 32mm scale as Warhammer 40,000. Models are fully interchangeable between Kill Team and 40k at the same base size.
printingTips: Same settings as 40k. Kill Team features fewer models with more detail — resin is ideal for specialist operatives. FDM works for terrain.
popularWith: Skirmish gamers, 40k players, narrative gamers

name: Necromunda
description: Necromunda is a gang warfare skirmish game set in the underhive of a grimdark megacity, where rival gangs fight for territory and resources.
scaleNotes: Uses the same 32mm scale as Warhammer 40,000. Features gangers, hangers-on, and industrial terrain.
printingTips: 32mm gangers benefit from 0.2mm nozzle for facial detail. Industrial terrain (gang hideouts, sector mechanicus) prints beautifully on FDM.
popularWith: Narrative gamers, terrain builders, Necromunda lore fans

name: Warcry
description: Warcry is a fast-paced fantasy skirmish game set in the Age of Sigmar universe, where warbands from the eight realms clash in brutal combat.
scaleNotes: Uses the same 32mm scale as Age of Sigmar. Models are fully interchangeable between Warcry and AoS at the same base size.
printingTips: 32mm warband models print well on FDM. Terrain pieces like ruined temples and chaos shrines are excellent FDM subjects.
popularWith: Skirmish gamers, AoS players, terrain builders

name: Star Wars: X-Wing
description: Star Wars: X-Wing is a miniatures game of space combat where players pilot iconic Star Wars ships in fast-paced dogfights.
scaleNotes: 1:27 ratio scale (59.3mm eye-level, 64.8mm top-of-head). Ships are the focus — no infantry-scale miniatures.
printingTips: 1:27 ships are large enough for FDM to handle detail well. Use 0.2mm nozzle for cockpit and panel line detail. Large ships like the Millennium Falcon benefit from 0.4mm nozzle.
popularWith: Star Wars fans, space combat enthusiasts, model builders

name: Conquest: Last Argument of Kings
description: Conquest is a mass-battle fantasy wargame with a unique alternating activation system, featuring the 100 Kingdoms, Nords, Dweghom, and other factions.
scaleNotes: 35mm scale, same as Star Wars: Legion. Larger than Warhammer's 32mm, providing more canvas for detail and painterly expression.
printingTips: 35mm infantry benefits from 0.2mm nozzle at 0.06mm layer height. Large monsters and cavalry print well on FDM at 0.2mm layers.
popularWith: Fantasy wargamers, army builders, painters
